architecture_decisions: - `SourceLineageStore` should depend on two explicit persistence protocols: immutable object storage and transactional lineage metadata.
work_items: - `SourceLineageStore` should be designed to persist source files using SHA-256 digests in immutable object storage, and lineage manifests and heads using durable current-lineage heads in a transactional metadata store.
validations: - The `SourceLineageStore` should ensure that source files are persisted using SHA-256 digests in immutable object storage, and lineage manifests and heads are persisted using durable current-lineage heads in a transactional metadata store.

AC-01: validate protected requirement — Durable lineage accepts the same canonical lowercase UUID Project/run identity as #60. `Project.id` + `EngineeringRun.id` remain the only integration inputs; `project:<id>`, `workspace_ref`, paths, URLs, caller/model storage keys and malformed identity cannot become durable storage authority.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — `SourceLineageStore` requires explicit durable object and metadata adapters and exposes no filesystem state-root parameter. `ProjectWorkspaceAllocator` requires an explicit lineage store and uses its local protected root only for generated disposable leases; no `/tmp` or other local path is considered accepted durable lineage state.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — Every source file is persisted by SHA-256 through an immutable write-if-absent object contract. The Vercel production adapter uses the public Python SDK with `access="private"`, deterministic digest-derived paths, no random suffix, no overwrite and read-after-write/read-time digest verification. Missing, corrupt or conflicting content fails closed.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — Canonical lineage manifests and the current Project/run lineage head persist in the relational boundary. Manifest insertion and head advancement are transactional. Advancement succeeds only when the durable current lineage exactly equals the expected parent (or is absent for initialization), so separate API invocations/instances cannot accept different children from one parent.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — A different stale child is rejected without changing the accepted head; unchanged source cannot create a lineage; and retrying the exact already-accepted initialization or implementation child returns the existing lineage idempotently after `SourceLineageStore`/allocator process recreation.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — Any accepted historical/current lineage can be resolved and reconstructed into a fresh disposable workspace using durable manifest metadata and immutable objects. Manifest checksum/shape/identity tampering, identity mismatch, missing/corrupt objects, object size mismatch or reconstructed content-digest mismatch fails before the lineage is used.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — A failed or partial durable object write cannot create or advance accepted lineage metadata. A failed/losing metadata CAS cannot advance the durable head and rolls back its unaccepted manifest metadata. Unreferenced immutable objects may remain but are never reported as accepted lineage.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Materialized workspaces remain generated server-owned leases beneath a configured local root, never durable state. Cleanup is idempotent and deletes only the lease; a separate allocator/function instance with a different local root can reconstruct the same accepted lineage from durable storage afterward.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Existing source count/per-file/aggregate/path/provenance bounds remain enforced. Lineage/workspace evidence contains bounded canonical IDs, lineage/content/provenance digests, counts/sizes and generated lease identity only; it contains no source bytes, filesystem roots, provider tokens/raw state, generic shell/Git/HTTP authority, protected-stage self-approval, production-promotion or deployment authority.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — The worker delivers the forward migration, official Vercel Python SDK dependency, durable adapters, refactored #60 store/allocator and focused durability tests without provisioning resources or applying the migration. The exact candidate passes the deterministic workstream-spec gate, full API regression, Parallax P2 CI and Bounded Autonomy Pilot and targets `integration/wave2-app-builder` READY FOR INTEGRATION without merge/deploy.
risks: - The risk of introducing a new dependency on two separate persistence protocols could lead to increased complexity and potential integration issues with existing infrastructure.
